about.title: Angels Camp Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Angels Camp sees plenty of foot and vehicle traffic along Rt 49, Rt 4, S Main Street, and Murphys Grade Road, especially on Saturday afternoons when local shops and visitors are out in force. Defective products don't just cause harm on the road — a malfunctioning tool at a hardware store, a faulty vehicle part, or an unsafe piece of outdoor gear can lead to serious injury anywhere in town. Under California law, injured people often don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless; strict liability means showing the product itself was defective and that the defect caused harm. That's a meaningful difference for someone recovering from an injury and trying to understand their options. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects Angels Camp residents with independent attorneys who handle these claims on contingency. If a product failed you here in Calaveras foothill country, it's worth having someone look at what happened before evidence disappears or the product gets discarded.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Case
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact — rather than repairing, discarding, or losing it — can be critical evidence in showing what went wrong.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product had a defect and that defect caused your injury. This can simplify what you need to establish compared to a typical negligence claim.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought at a local Angels Camp store — who can be responsible?
items.answer: Potentially more than one party. Depending on how the defect arose, the manufacturer, distributor, or even the retailer that sold the product in Angels Camp could share responsibility. An independent attorney can help sort out which parties are involved in your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that caused my injury?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, without repairing or discarding it. The product itself is often key evidence, and losing it can make a claim harder to support later.
